name: Aartech Solonics Ltd
title: Aartech Solonics Ltd - 542580 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Small, debt-light energy-equipment firm (FY26 revenue ~Rs 40 cr, 12-15% organic growth) with no capacity or utilisation disclosure, vague guidance and an order book of only Rs 10 cr at year start, so the supply-side read is thin.

summary.headline: Aartech Solonics FY26 revenue reached Rs 40 Cr (record), with EBITDA roughly 3x FY25 as FY25 carried a ~Rs 4 Cr exceptional charge; order book guided to Rs 25 Cr by June 2026.
summary.overview: Management held its first virtual investor call for Q4 and FY26 and described FY26 as a record-turnover year with tighter expense control. Revenue was stated as Rs 40 Cr for 2025-26, with organic growth of about 12-15% a year and roughly doubled over five years. EBITDA and PAT were said to be about 3x FY25, which included an exceptional expense of about Rs 4 Cr. Management discussed new export wins (Indonesia BTS, Qatar and Oman, China and Africa for control and relay panels), defence trials, and a new Narmadapuram facility targeted for operations in early FY28. Specific Q4 quarterly figures were not given in the call.

segments.name: BTS 2000 (Bus Transfer System)
segments.commentary: Flagship product serving process industries, refineries and gencos; average margin stated at 35-40%. Life cycle moving from new supply to retrofitting. Won Indonesia project against ABB.

segments.name: Control and Relay Panels (CRP)
segments.commentary: Traditional bread-and-butter line since the 1980s; now moving into volumes via EPCs, but price-sensitive with tough margin competition. Exports started to China and Africa; plan to enter 220 kV market.

segments.name: Defence (AAPM, EMLS, rugged mil-grade)
segments.commentary: AAPM validated across Northern, Western and Southern Army commands; patent filed, expected in 12-18 months. Orders executed for Indian Navy and Air Force. Management sized the market at Rs 500 Cr+ and an addressable Rs 50-100 Cr for Aartech.

segments.name: Ultracapacitors (Faradigm subsidiary), Flywheel, Kranking, BestCase
segments.commentary: Ultracapacitors manufactured through subsidiary Faradigm Ultracapacitors. Flywheel still in development, with traction in data centres. BestCase industrial plastic enclosures serve retail through B2B.

guidance_outlook: Order book expected to reach around Rs 25 Cr by end of June 2026, from Rs 10 Cr at start of FY26 against ~Rs 15 Cr of bids outstanding.
New Narmadapuram renewable and power equipment facility: civil work in progress for 9-10 months; first operations expected early 2027, commercial operations targeted end FY27 or early FY28.
Management declined to give a numerical revenue, EBITDA or CAGR target; said it prefers to under-commit and over-deliver.
Inorganic growth opportunities are being explored, but no details were given.
Management expects organic growth in the 12-15% range to continue based on recent trends.
capex_capacity: Two manufacturing units (Mandideep, Madhya Pradesh and Parwanoo, Himachal Pradesh), plus one upcoming unit at Narmadapuram via a wholly owned subsidiary.
Narmadapuram land awarded by MP Government in 2025 within a renewable and power equipment cluster, about 90 km from Bhopal; foundation stone laid.
Planned product focus at the new facility: next-generation energy storage for renewables, defence and transportation.
demand_pricing: Government power-sector investment flowing into T&D is driving CRP demand; government push for local manufacturing is giving an edge.
Middle East (Qatar, Oman) utilities and EPCs such as Jindal and TRAGS have bought BTS and Fault Current Limiter products.
Competition in CRP from Siemens, Schneider and ABB; price-sensitive and margin-pressured.
Defence has high entry barriers and long trial and validation cycles, but offers good margins if products are made in India.
Working capital is high, with 120-180 day projects and about five months from order to invoicing.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment (BTS 2000, ultracapacitors, CRP, defence) has the highest long-term scalability and margin, and what revenue scale is possible in 2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said defence is a sunrise segment with good margins but long gestation. Addressable market is Rs 500 Cr+, and for Aartech's current size, Rs 50-100 Cr. No segment-wise revenue forecast was given.

qa_highlights.question: What margins are earned on Middle East orders, and what is the export share?
qa_highlights.answer: BTS 2000 average margin of about 35-40%. Export share about 10% of FY26 revenue; geopolitical uncertainty makes targets difficult.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth trajectory and margin range for FY27 and the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is at multiple inflection points and expects organic traction to continue. It declined to give CAGR or margin targets, and said inorganic growth is being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating leverage expand margins as growth continues?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins vary by product. BTS 2000 at 35-40% tapers to 10-15% net across competitive products. Innovation is seen as the leverage, with a pipeline of R&D investments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 10 Cr at start of FY26, Rs 15 Cr of bids outstanding, and an expected order book of about Rs 25 Cr by end-June 2026. Timelines depend on bid results.

risks_watch: Revenue and EBITDA are not quantified for FY26 in the call, and no Q4 standalone figures were given; verify against the filed results.
Export and geopolitical uncertainty affecting Middle East and Africa orders.
Margin dilution outside BTS 2000 (CRP price competition); net margin of 10-15% stated.
Narmadapuram facility timing (early FY28 commercial operations) and capex funding.
Defence revenue depends on trials, validations and patents (AAPM patent expected in 12-18 months).
Working capital intensity and negative operating cash flow in some periods.
Management's refusal to give forward numerical targets; investor feedback was raised on this point.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on strategy and innovation but evasive on forward numbers, repeatedly declining to give revenue, margin or CAGR targets. It spoke broadly on defence and export potential and kept guidance to the order book (Rs 25 Cr by June).
key_quotes: So, as we can see that, if we compare year on year, FY25 and FY26, we are definitely at a much better page than what we were last year because we have not just achieved a record turnover in this year.
We are trying to basically work on a principle of under-committing and over-delivering.
As of the beginning of the financial year, we had around Rs. 10 crores of order book in hand.

financial_highlights.change: Record turnover; roughly doubled over five years, organic growth ~12-15% p.a.
Described as ~3x FY25, which had ~Rs 4 Cr exceptional expense

financial_highlights.value: Nil on books; only cash credit facilities for working capital
Steady returns of about 5-10% a year (bonus and dividend)
35-40% average (gross, as stated); net 10-15% across portfolio

financial_highlights.metric: Order book at start of FY26

adds.what: New Narmadapuram renewable and power equipment facility (via wholly owned subsidiary); civil work in progress

growth.why: Management expects organic growth of 12-15% to continue, backed by an order book guided to about Rs 25 Cr by June 2026 (from Rs 10 Cr at start of FY26) and a Narmadapuram plant targeted for commercial operations end FY27 or early FY28, though no numerical revenue target was given and Q4 quarterly figures were not disclosed.
